s01 — baseline vs. iterative mapping (chr19, SNP-only)

knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE, fig.align = "center")
library(ggplot2); library(dplyr); library(tidyr); library(readr)
source("analyses/lib/design.r")   # bartheme(), corecol(); knit from the project root

Provenance

  • Rendered from commit 12452f63e370 (branch mason2-sims) on 2026-10-28 10:27
  • This notebook: notebook as committed

  • Each data file’s producing script and command: the section’s MANIFEST.yaml

1 Question & design

Does iterative (pseudo-it) mapping recover more true divergence than single-shot mapping, and does that depend on the variant caller? A diverged sample is simulated against the mm39 reference, mapped back, and variant-called; reference bias is the true divergence that gets lost. Iterative mapping remaps to a consensus that absorbs the recovered divergence, lowering the effective divergence each round.

Everything below is chr19, SNP-only, 30×, produced by workflow.smk (divergence recovery), het_recovery.smk (het), and read_classification.smk (read placement), all driven by config/config.yaml and launched with the run_*.sh orchestrators.

  • Truth (analyses/lib/make_truth_vcf.py): homozygous divergence SNPs at rate D ∈ {0.02, 0.04, 0.06, 0.08, 0.10} (+ a D=0 control), genotype 1|1; heterozygous SNPs at rate H = 0.005, genotype 0|1; no indels (indel_divergence = 0, the SNP-only baseline). Alt alleles are drawn uniformly from the 3 non-reference bases, independently per site (a phylogenetic extension would instead inherit alleles down a tree).
  • Reads (mason_simulator): chr19 extracted from mm39 (samtools faidx); 30×, 150 bp paired reads, 300 bp mean fragment; NFRAG = cov × len / (2 × readlen). 3 replicate seeds — 42, 43, 44 (independent truth + reads); figures show mean ± 1 SD.
  • Mapping & iteration: bwa mem (defaults) → samtools sort/index. n_iterations = 3; iteration 1 maps to the reference (the single-shot baseline), iteration k maps to the consensus from iteration k−1. The consensus is bcftools consensus of that iteration’s homozygous SNP calls only (bcftools view -v snps -g hom) — which keeps it exactly reference-length (identity coordinates → no liftover) and free of IUPAC het codes.
  • Variant callers (an axis; each iterates independently): gatk HaplotypeCaller (reference-anchored local reassembly; run scatter-gather over 8 intervals → GenotypeGVCFs), bcftools mpileup | call (pileup), freebayes (haplotype-from-alignment). Min mapping quality 20; all output normalized identically (bcftools norm -f ref -m- --atomize).
  • Scoring: divergence recovery (cumulative) = exact consensus-vs-reference SNP diff (consensus_diff_snps.py) scored vs normalized truth with compare_vcfs.py (div_tp); het recovery and the het/other fate bands = compare_vcfs.py on the raw caller VCF (calls.norm, which carries the 0/1 genotypes) vs truth (het_tp, div_het, div_other); read placement = mason -oa truth alignment regenerated at the original seed (deterministic → identical reads) and each iteration’s BAM classified with compare_bams.py (exact / shifted / soft-clipped / mismapped / unmapped; 150 bp tolerance). Each read’s true position is its start on its source haplotype (mason’s oP tag) mapped back to the reference (analyses/lib/truth_haplotypes.py). Placement is judged against where an aligner would lay the read down unclipped: the start of the best alignment of its leftmost 30 bases on that haplotype (bwa mem scores), which moves it 1–3 bp off oP only for the ~0.02% of reads with a sequencing indel among those bases. Tables before 2026-10-27 took the position from the truth BAM’s alignment start/CIGAR instead, which is 1–3 bp off for ~1% of reads here (mason writes dense SNP clusters as fake deletion-insertion pairs) and for ~32% of reads in s02; tables made at commit 8762eab (also 2026-10-27, before this rule) placed every read at oP.
# --- divergence recovery (from the consensus-vs-reference diff) ---
d <- read_csv("analyses/s01-baseline-iterative/results/s01-base-iterative-summary.csv") %>%
  filter(divergence > 0) %>%                       # no divergence sites at D=0
  mutate(recall    = div_tp / n_truth_div,
         precision = ifelse(n_called_snp > 0, 1 - fp / n_called_snp, NA),
         caller    = factor(caller, levels = c("gatk", "bcftools", "freebayes")),
         iteration = factor(iteration))
agg <- d %>% group_by(caller, divergence, iteration) %>%
  summarize(recall_m = mean(recall), recall_sd = sd(recall),
            prec_m = mean(precision), prec_sd = sd(precision), .groups = "drop")
n_iter <- max(as.integer(as.character(d$iteration)))
cols   <- corecol(pal = "wilke", numcol = n_iter)

# --- het recovery + fate bands (from the raw per-iteration caller VCF) ---
het <- read_csv("analyses/s01-baseline-iterative/results/s01-base-het-recovery-by-iter.csv") %>%
  mutate(caller = factor(caller, levels = c("gatk", "bcftools", "freebayes")),
         iteration = factor(iteration),
         het_recall = het_tp / n_truth_het)   # D=0 KEPT: het recall at D=0 = the germline baseline
hets <- het %>% group_by(caller, divergence, iteration) %>%
  summarize(m = mean(het_recall), s = sd(het_recall), .groups = "drop")

# --- read placement ---
rc <- read_csv("analyses/s01-baseline-iterative/results/s01-base-readclass-by-iter.csv") %>%
  mutate(caller = factor(caller, levels = c("gatk", "bcftools", "freebayes")),
         iteration = factor(iteration))   # D=0 KEPT: near-all-exact mapping baseline

# --- fate of divergent sites (cumulative-correct) ---
# Recovered comes from the CONSENSUS (d$div_tp), because a site recovered in one round is
# baked into the consensus and no longer re-called the next -- so the raw caller VCF would
# wrongly show it migrating back to "lost". The het/other bands (sites the caller calls
# 0/1 or wrong-allele, hence NOT baked into the hom consensus) come from the caller VCF;
# lost-to-reference is the remainder.
fate <- inner_join(
    d   %>% select(caller, divergence, seed, iteration, n_truth_div, rec = div_tp),
    het %>% select(caller, divergence, seed, iteration, div_het, div_other),
    by = c("caller", "divergence", "seed", "iteration")) %>%
  mutate(lost = pmax(n_truth_div - rec - div_het - div_other, 0)) %>%
  group_by(caller, divergence, iteration) %>%
  summarize(Recovered           = mean(rec / n_truth_div),
            `Called het`        = mean(div_het / n_truth_div),
            `Lost to reference` = mean(lost / n_truth_div),
            Other               = mean(div_other / n_truth_div), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_longer(-c(caller, divergence, iteration), names_to = "fate", values_to = "prop") %>%
  mutate(fate = factor(fate, levels = c("Recovered", "Called het",
                                        "Lost to reference", "Other")))

small_legend <- theme(legend.position = "bottom",
                      legend.text = element_text(size = 8),
                      legend.title = element_blank(),
                      legend.key.size = unit(0.40, "cm"))

2 Read classification

The mapping-side view: where did each read actually land relative to where it was simulated from? Each stacked bar is the composition of read placements at one iteration (exact / shifted / soft-clipped / span-off / mismapped / diff-chr / unmapped), for every caller (rows) and divergence (columns). Iteration 1 maps to the reference and so is caller-independent; later iterations map to each caller’s own consensus. span_off = correct start, but the read’s reference footprint is >10 bp off its true one; ≤0.004% of reads here (a class of its own only since the 2026-10-27 tables; before, these reads counted as exact).

classes <- c("exact", "shifted", "clipped", "span_off", "mismapped", "diff_chr", "unmapped", "missing")
class_cols <- c(exact = "#009E73", shifted = "#56B4E9", clipped = "#E69F00", span_off = "#F0E442",
                mismapped = "#D55E00", diff_chr = "#CC79A7",
                unmapped = "#999999", missing = "#333333")
comp <- rc %>% group_by(caller, divergence, iteration) %>%
  summarize(across(all_of(paste0(classes, "_prop")), mean), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_longer(-c(caller, divergence, iteration), names_to = "class", values_to = "prop") %>%
  mutate(class = factor(sub("_prop", "", class), levels = classes))

ggplot(comp, aes(x = iteration, y = prop, fill = class)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.85) +
  facet_grid(caller ~ divergence) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = class_cols) +
  xlab("Iteration") + ylab("Fraction of reads") +
  bartheme() + small_legend

Interpretation. Read the iter1 bars across the three caller rows — they are identical: single-shot mapping is caller-independent (everyone maps to the reference), and at D=0.10 only ~57% of reads are exact, ~40% soft-clipped. That is the key control — the reads are placed the same way for every caller at iter1, yet gatk recovers far fewer SNPs (§3) — so gatk’s single-shot deficit is its reference-anchored reassembler, not a mapping/clipping artifact. From iter2 the rows separate: bcftools/freebayes recover ~all divergence at iter1, so their consensus is near-complete and reads map almost perfectly by iter2; gatk’s consensus improves gradually, so its soft-clip band shrinks gradually (~40%→10% at D=0.10). Mapping quality is downstream of caller recovery (recover → consensus → better mapping → recover more), and the soft-clipped bases are retained in the BAM and used by gatk anyway — so this is a readout of falling effective divergence, not evidence removed from the caller.

3 SNP recovery

The homozygous-divergence result — the core reference-bias question — from four angles: the fate of every divergent site, the recovered counts, recall/precision, and how the iteration benefit differs by caller.

3.1 Fate of divergent sites per iteration

Every true divergent site is homozygous-alternate and should be recovered as such; these stacked bars show what actually becomes of it at each iteration — the variant-calling analogue of the read-placement composition above. Recovered = the site is in the consensus (cumulative); Called het / Other = the raw caller VCF calls it 0/1 or with the wrong allele (so it is not baked into the hom consensus); Lost to reference = the remainder (the sample looks like the reference — reference bias itself).

fate_cols <- c("Recovered" = "#009e73", "Called het" = "#56b4e9",
               "Lost to reference" = "#d55e00", "Other" = "#999999")
ggplot(fate, aes(x = iteration, y = prop, fill = fate)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.85) +
  facet_grid(caller ~ divergence) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = fate_cols) +
  xlab("Iteration") + ylab("Proportion of true divergent sites") +
  bartheme() + small_legend

Interpretation. The orange Lost to reference band is reference bias, and it shrinks every iteration — most dramatically for gatk at high divergence (28% → 18% lost at D=0.10). The Called het band (a divergent site only partly rescued — one allele’s worth of reads surviving) stays thin throughout (~0.5%). bcftools/freebayes are almost fully green from iteration 1; gatk starts with a large lost band that iteration steadily eats into. This is the recall story below shown as a complete accounting of where every divergent site goes.

3.2 Recovered SNP counts

True divergent SNPs recovered, shown as count (% of truth, +new), by caller and divergence for each iteration (means over the 3 seeds). +new = additional true SNPs recovered vs. the previous iteration (blank for iter1, the single-shot baseline); truth = total divergent sites simulated. Rows are grouped by caller.

library(kableExtra)
fmt <- function(x) formatC(round(x), format = "d", big.mark = ",")
cells <- d %>%
  group_by(caller, divergence, iteration) %>%
  summarize(recovered = mean(div_tp),
            recall    = mean(div_tp / n_truth_div), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(caller, divergence, iteration) %>%
  group_by(caller, divergence) %>%
  mutate(gained = recovered - lag(recovered)) %>%   # new SNPs vs previous iteration
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(cell = ifelse(is.na(gained),
                       sprintf("%s (%.1f%%)", fmt(recovered), 100 * recall),
                       sprintf("%s (%.1f%%, +%s)", fmt(recovered), 100 * recall, fmt(gained))),
         iteration = paste0("iter", iteration)) %>%
  select(caller, divergence, iteration, cell) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = iteration, values_from = cell)

truth_col <- d %>% group_by(caller, divergence) %>%
  summarize(truth = formatC(round(mean(n_truth_div)), format = "d", big.mark = ","),
            .groups = "drop")
tab <- left_join(truth_col, cells, by = c("caller", "divergence")) %>%
  arrange(caller, divergence)

grp  <- tab %>% count(caller)
disp <- tab %>% select(-caller)
kbl <- knitr::kable(
    disp, align = "r",
    col.names = c("divergence", "truth", paste0("iter", seq_len(n_iter))),
    caption = "True divergent SNPs recovered as count (% of truth), mean over seeds.") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
                full_width = FALSE, position = "center")
start <- 1
for (i in seq_len(nrow(grp))) {
  kbl   <- kbl %>% pack_rows(as.character(grp$caller[i]), start, start + grp$n[i] - 1)
  start <- start + grp$n[i]
}

3.3 Precision and recall

Recall (recovered / truth) and precision (of the consensus SNP set vs truth), by caller. At each divergence the grey connector spans the iterations, so its length is the iteration gain; error bars are ±1 SD over the 3 seeds.

ggplot(agg, aes(x = factor(divergence), y = recall_m, color = iteration)) +
  geom_line(aes(group = divergence), color = "grey65", size = 0.6) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = recall_m - recall_sd, ymax = recall_m + recall_sd), width = 0.0015) +
  geom_point(size = 2.6) +
  facet_wrap(~caller) +
  scale_x_discrete(guide = guide_axis(angle = 45)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  scale_color_manual(values = cols, name = "Iteration") +
  xlab("Simulated divergence (D)") + ylab("SNP divergence recall") +
  bartheme() + theme(legend.position = "bottom")

ggplot(agg, aes(x = factor(divergence), y = prec_m, color = iteration)) +
  geom_line(aes(group = divergence), color = "grey65", size = 0.6) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = prec_m - prec_sd, ymax = prec_m + prec_sd), width = 0.0015) +
  geom_point(size = 2.6) +
  facet_wrap(~caller) +
  scale_x_discrete(guide = guide_axis(angle = 45)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  scale_color_manual(values = cols, name = "Iteration") +
  xlab("Simulated divergence (D)") + ylab("SNP precision (consensus vs truth)") +
  bartheme() + theme(legend.position = "bottom")

Interpretation. Recall rises every iteration and converges by ~3 rounds; the effect is tiny for bcftools / freebayes (already ~99% — little headroom) and large for gatk, whose single-shot recall collapses at high divergence but is substantially rescued. Error bars are <0.1 pt everywhere (aggregate recall over chr19’s millions of sites is near-deterministic — the near-zero seed variance is itself a result). Precision confirms the recall gains are not bought with false positives.

3.4 Truth-site check: every truth SNP is in the reads

A truth SNP that mason never simulated into the reads (a phantom) could not be recovered by any caller or iteration, so it would belong out of the recall denominator. analyses/lib/effective_truth.py checks every truth SNP (run_effective_truth.sh, every divergence with a truth BAM, seed 42):

  • Haplotypes: mason’s two haplotypes are rebuilt from the mason-format truth VCF (analyses/lib/truth_haplotypes.py; byte-identical to mason_materializer’s at D = 0.10).
  • Bases: each truth read’s base at a SNP is read from the read’s position on its source haplotype (mason -oa tags oH, oP). No alignment is involved.
  • Reads used: only reads consistent with their haplotype (mismatches away from truth SNPs no more than mason’s error count XE); reads from the haplotype(s) carrying the alt.
  • Phantom: at least 5 such reads and fewer than 10% presenting the alt.
ph <- read_csv("analyses/s01-baseline-iterative/results/effective-truth/phantom-by-divergence.csv",
               col_types = cols())
n_ph <- sum(ph$n_phantom_div + ph$n_phantom_het)
ph %>% transmute(divergence, `truth SNPs` = n_truth_snp,
                 `phantom (div / het)` = sprintf("%d / %d", n_phantom_div, n_phantom_het),
                 `lowest alt fraction` = min_alt_frac,
                 `reads consistent` = scales::percent(frac_reads_consistent, accuracy = 0.1),
                 `old method flags (div / het)` = sprintf("%d / %d", n_cigar_flag_div, n_cigar_flag_het)) %>%
  kable(caption = "Truth-site check per divergence. 'Lowest alt fraction' is over all judged SNPs; the last column is what the earlier, alignment-based scan flagged.",
        table.attr = 'class="center"')

Interpretation. No truth SNP at any divergence is a phantom: at every judged site the reads from the alt-carrying haplotypes present the alt (lowest alt fraction 0.6). Recall in this notebook is therefore the true recall of what was simulated, and no correction is applied. Earlier versions reported a small “phantom floor” (up to 0.6% at D = 0.10), explained as mason dropping one of two adjacent variants, and a phantom-corrected “effective recall”. Both came from an artifact of the old scan, which read bases through mason’s -oa alignment strings: mason writes dense SNP clusters there as fake deletion-insertion pairs, so bases landed one position off and real alt sites looked like the reference. The last column reproduces the old flags; none is a phantom.

3.5 Variant caller comparison

Where iteration helps most: the recall improvement from single-shot (iter1) to the last iteration, by caller and divergence.

gain <- agg %>%
  filter(iteration %in% c("1", as.character(n_iter))) %>%
  select(caller, divergence, iteration, recall_m) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = iteration, values_from = recall_m) %>%
  mutate(gain = .data[[as.character(n_iter)]] - .data[["1"]])

ggplot(gain, aes(x = factor(divergence), y = caller, fill = gain)) +
  scale_x_discrete(guide = guide_axis(angle = 45)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", size = 0.6) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("+%.1f", gain * 100)), size = 3.4) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#f7f7f7", high = "#0072b2",
                      labels = scales::percent, name = "Recall gain\n(iter1 -> last)") +
  xlab("Simulated divergence (D)") + ylab(NULL) +
  bartheme() + theme(axis.line = element_blank(), axis.ticks = element_blank())

Interpretation. The gain is inversely related to how good the caller already is, and scales with divergence: near-zero for the pileup/haplotype callers, rising to a large lift for gatk at high divergence — iteration lowers the effective divergence so gatk’s reference-anchored assembly (which fails on far-from-reference sequence) starts working again. Iteration mitigates reference bias exactly where single-shot suffers most.

3.6 Per-variant read fate: why a SNP is (not) called — whole chromosome

Everything above measures recovery in aggregate; this section asks, per variant and directly at the reference base, why each SNP is called or not — on every hom-div SNP on chr19 (no sampling; 2.46M sites at D=0.04 up to 6.14M at D=0.10). This is the project’s standard per-variant read-fate analysis (analyses/lib/variant_read_fate.py, run in --aggregate mode across all callers × divergences by run_vrf_aggregate.sh; figures rebuilt below from its summary tables).

Definitions / assumptions. For each true divergent SNP we take every read that truly covers its reference coordinate p and classify what that read does at p:

  • Covering reads — reads whose true (mason-simulated) fragment spans p, assigned from the -oa truth BAM (i.e. from where the read came from, not where bwa put it) — so reads that were lost, mismapped, or unmapped are still counted in the denominator. A read’s true span is its interval on its source haplotype (oP tag, read length) mapped back to the reference, not the truth BAM’s alignment start/CIGAR (see Methods).
  • True allele via oH — mason tags each read with its source haplotype (oH); with the phased genotype this gives each read’s true allele independent of sequencing error. For hom 1|1 SNPs both haplotypes carry the alt, so n_true_alt = all covering reads (verified exactly). (For a het 0|1 site — see s03 — the alt is on one haplotype, so n_true_alt is only the ~half of covering reads from that haplotype.)
  • f_alt = (reads with the alt aligned at p) / n_true_alt — of the reads that truly carry the alt, the fraction that actually deliver it at the correct coordinate. A read whose start is shifted but whose SNP base still aligns at p counts (verified: shifted reads present the true alt, never a displaced base). It is alt-support survival, not the pileup allele fraction: the denominator is restricted to the alt-carrying reads, so f_alt = 1 under unbiased mapping and drops below 1 only when those reads are lost (clipped / mismapped / unmapped). At a het site this means f_alt is ≈1 by construction unless the alt-haplotype reads drop out — it is not the ~0.5 you would get from ref+alt.
  • What is at p (one class per covering read): alt / ref / other-base (error) aligned there; clipped over p / deleted at p (read at the locus but nothing aligned at p); mapped elsewhere / unmapped (read never reaches p). Read-start placement (exact/shifted) is deliberately collapsed — only what happens at p matters.
library(ggalluvial)
AGG <- "analyses/s01-baseline-iterative/results/vrf-agg"        # aggregate tables from run_vrf_aggregate.sh
lv  <- c("gatk", "bcftools", "freebayes")
hcomp <- bind_rows(lapply(list.files(AGG, "hcomp.csv$", full.names = TRUE), read_csv, col_types = cols())) %>%
  mutate(caller = factor(caller, levels = lv))                  # per (caller,div,iter,call-status): at-p read-fate sums
gtraj <- bind_rows(lapply(list.files(AGG, "gtraj.csv$", full.names = TRUE), read_csv, col_types = cols()))

3.6.1 Why do SNPs stay uncalled?

For the SNPs a caller does not call, is the alt actually there (alt maps at p)? If yes, the caller — not the mapping — is the blocker.

hcomp %>% filter(status == "not_called", iteration %in% c(1, 3)) %>%
  mutate(alt_frac = alt_at_p / n_reads) %>%
  ggplot(aes(factor(divergence), alt_frac, color = caller, linetype = factor(iteration),
             group = interaction(caller, iteration))) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) + geom_point(size = 2.4) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, limits = c(0, 1)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = corecol(pal = "wilke", numcol = 3), name = "caller") +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c(`1` = "solid", `3` = "22"), name = "iteration") +
  labs(x = "divergence (D)", y = "alt maps at p  (fraction of covering reads)",
       title = "Not-called SNPs: is the base there? (whole chromosome, every hom-div SNP)") +
  bartheme()

Interpretation. Two clean bands. For gatk, not-called SNPs have the alt presented ~76–87% of the time across all divergences — the base is right there and the reassembler still won’t call it (assembler-limited). For bcftools / freebayes it is only ~16–32% — a pileup/haplotype caller misses a SNP essentially only when the base genuinely isn’t presented (alignment-limited).

3.6.2 What maps at position p (composition)

The full read-fate breakdown at the highest divergence (D=0.10), by caller (columns) and call outcome (rows). Read this at p: alt maps at p is the base being delivered; everything else is a way it isn’t.

cats <- c("alt_at_p", "ref_at_p", "err_at_p", "clipped", "deleted", "mapped_elsewhere", "unmapped")
nice <- c(alt_at_p = "alt maps at p", ref_at_p = "ref maps at p", err_at_p = "other base (error)",
          clipped = "clipped over p", deleted = "deleted at p",
          mapped_elsewhere = "mapped elsewhere", unmapped = "unmapped")
fcol <- setNames(c("#1b7837", "#2166ac", "#92c5de", "#e08214", "#8073ac", "#b2182b", "#4d4d4d"),
                 unname(nice[cats]))
hcomp %>% filter(divergence == 0.10) %>%
  pivot_longer(all_of(cats), names_to = "atp", values_to = "reads") %>%
  mutate(frac = reads / n_reads, atp = factor(nice[atp], levels = unname(nice[cats])),
         status = recode(status, called = "called", not_called = "not called")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(factor(iteration), frac, fill = atp)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.75, color = "grey30", linewidth = 0.12) + facet_grid(status ~ caller) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = fcol, name = "what is at position p") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(x = "iteration", y = "fraction of covering reads",
       title = "What maps at p — D=0.10, whole chromosome, by caller and call outcome") +
  bartheme()

Interpretation. The not-called row is the story. gatk’s box is green (alt maps at p, ~76%) — the reads deliver the base. bcftools/freebayes are red + orange (mapped elsewhere ~40–53%, clipped ~15%) — the base isn’t presented, dominated by reads that mismapped or were clipped. Called SNPs converge to ~99.5% alt maps at p by iteration 3 for all three.

3.6.3 Joint state across iterations (G)

Each SNP flows through its joint (call status × f_alt bin) state per iteration. Within every panel the lower box is called, the upper box not called (thin gap between); colour bands are the f_alt bin (viridis; yellow = high, i.e. alt well-presented at p). Rows are callers, columns are divergence — all conditions, whole chromosome. (Larger single-condition versions, with the box labels, are also written to results/vrf-viz-full/G_<caller>_D<div>.png.)

BIN   <- c("0.0-0.2", "0.2-0.4", "0.4-0.6", "0.6-0.8", "0.8-1.0")
fbcol <- setNames(hcl.colors(5, "Viridis"), BIN)
Glev  <- c(paste("not called", BIN, sep = " · "), "gap", paste("called", BIN, sep = " · "))
makeG <- function(cc, dd, showlab = TRUE) {
  g <- gtraj %>% filter(caller == cc, divergence == dd, fb1 %in% BIN, fb2 %in% BIN, fb3 %in% BIN)
  lodes <- g %>% mutate(id = row_number()) %>%
    pivot_longer(c(s1, fb1, s2, fb2, s3, fb3), names_to = c(".value", "iter"),
                 names_pattern = "([a-z]+)([0-9])") %>%
    transmute(id, n = n_snps, iter, status = ifelse(s == "not_called", "not called", "called"),
              fb = factor(fb, levels = BIN),
              state = factor(paste(status, fb, sep = " · "), levels = Glev), is_gap = FALSE)
  gapN <- round(0.03 * sum(g$n_snps))
  lodes <- bind_rows(lodes, tibble(id = max(lodes$id) + 1, n = gapN, iter = c("1", "2", "3"),
                     status = "gap", fb = factor(NA, levels = BIN),
                     state = factor("gap", levels = Glev), is_gap = TRUE))
  box <- lodes %>% filter(!is_gap) %>% group_by(iter, status) %>% summarize(n = sum(n), .groups = "drop") %>%
    group_by(iter) %>% mutate(ncall = sum(n[status == "called"])) %>% ungroup() %>%
    mutate(pos = as.integer(iter), xmin = pos - 0.22, xmax = pos + 0.22,
           ymin = ifelse(status == "called", 0, ncall + gapN),
           ymax = ifelse(status == "called", ncall, ncall + gapN + n), yc = (ymin + ymax) / 2)
  p <- ggplot(lodes, aes(x = iter, stratum = state, alluvium = id, y = n, fill = fb, alpha = is_gap)) +
    geom_flow() +
    geom_rect(data = box, aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax), inherit.aes = FALSE, fill = "white") +
    geom_stratum(color = NA, width = 0.44) +
    geom_rect(data = box, aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax), inherit.aes = FALSE, fill = NA, color = "grey15", linewidth = 0.6)
  if (showlab)
    p <- p + geom_text(data = box, aes(x = pos, y = yc, label = status), inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 2.5, fontface = "bold", colour = "grey10")
  p + scale_alpha_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = 0.4, `TRUE` = 0), guide = "none") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = fbcol, name = "f_alt bin", na.value = "white", na.translate = FALSE) +
    scale_x_discrete(labels = c("i1", "i2", "i3"), expand = c(0.08, 0.08)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, title = sprintf("%s  D=%s", cc, format(dd))) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 9) + theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), axis.text.y = element_blank(),
                                         plot.title = element_text(size = 9))
}
conds <- expand.grid(dd = c(0.005, 0.02, 0.04, 0.06, 0.08, 0.10), cc = lv, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)  # rows=caller, cols=div
patchwork::wrap_plots(Map(function(cc, dd) makeG(cc, dd, showlab = FALSE), conds$cc, conds$dd),
                      ncol = 6, guides = "collect")

Interpretation. The caller split is visible in every column: gatk’s not called box (upper) carries a big yellow (high f_alt) band at all divergences — base present, uncalled (assembler ceiling) — whereas bcftools/freebayes not called boxes are the low bins (base absent, alignment-limited), and that low-bin mass grows with divergence. All three called boxes (lower) fill toward yellow across iterations as placement tidies. Divergence runs left→right: the not-called block grows and its f_alt structure shifts down for the pileup/haplotype callers, while gatk’s stays high.

Data dictionary — results/vrf-agg/vrf-agg-<caller>-<div>-{gtraj,hcomp}.csv. Aggregate summaries over the whole chromosome; no per-SNP rows are stored.

  • -hcomp.csv — one row per (divergence, caller, iteration, status∈{called,not_called}). Columns alt_at_p, ref_at_p, err_at_p, clipped, deleted, mapped_elsewhere, unmapped are read counts summed over all SNPs (what maps at p); n_reads is their total (all covering reads). Fractions = column / n_reads.
  • -gtraj.csv — one row per distinct 3-iteration trajectory of (s{k}=call status, fb{k}=f_alt bin) with n_snps = number of SNPs that followed it. f_alt bins are 0.2-wide (0.0-0.2 … 0.8-1.0); s{k} ∈ {called, not_called}. Feeds figure G.

3.6.4 Companion decomposition: what changes when a SNP flips to called?

f_alt is one-dimensional — alt-support survival — and by construction blind to the reference / contaminant reads at p, the depth, and the MAPQ. So when a SNP flips not-called→called we ask what else moved. We re-run the read-fate tool in --pileup mode on a 30k-SNP sample (run_vrf_pileup.sh), which adds the position-centric pileup at p — the caller’s-eye view of every read aligned over p — and two complementary mismap counts: mismapped-IN (mmin_*: reads aligned at p whose true span is elsewhere — foreign reads the ledger books at their home loci) and its corollary mismapped-OUT (reads that belong at p by truth but are mapped elsewhere or unmapped, mm_clip+mm_noclip+dc+un). We join consecutive iterations per SNP and compare the pileup across three fates — not-called→called (flip), called→called (stayed called), not-called→not-called (stayed not-called) — over all f_alt bins and all divergences, tracking depth, ref reads, mismapped-in, mismapped-out, MAPQ, and f_alt. The by-divergence and by-fate figures pool all SNPs in a group; only the last figure separates by f_alt bin.

PILE  <- "analyses/s01-baseline-iterative/results/vrf-pileup"
BINS  <- c("0.0-0.2", "0.2-0.4", "0.4-0.6", "0.6-0.8", "0.8-1.0")
FATES <- c("stayed not-called", "flip (→called)", "stayed called")
nbps <- read_csv("analyses/s01-baseline-iterative/results/neighborhood/neighborhood-per-snp.csv",
                 col_types = cols())                         # per-SNP unrecovered-neighbor load
pl <- bind_rows(lapply(list.files(PILE, "vrf-pileup-.*\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE),
                       read_csv, col_types = cols())) %>%
  left_join(select(nbps, caller, divergence, snp_pos, iteration, nb_unrec = n_unrecovered),
            by = c("caller", "divergence", "snp_pos", "iteration")) %>%
  mutate(caller = factor(caller, levels = c("gatk", "bcftools", "freebayes")),
         f_alt = ifelse(n_true_alt > 0, (ex_alt + sh_alt) / n_true_alt, NA_real_),
         called = recovered == 1)
mkpairs <- function(k) inner_join(filter(pl, iteration == k), filter(pl, iteration == k + 1),
                                  by = c("caller", "divergence", "snp_pos"), suffix = c("_a", "_b"))
pairs <- bind_rows(mkpairs(1), mkpairs(2)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(f_alt_a), !is.na(f_alt_b)) %>%
  mutate(grp = case_when(!called_a &  called_b ~ "flip (→called)",
                          called_a &  called_b ~ "stayed called",
                         !called_a & !called_b ~ "stayed not-called",
                          TRUE ~ "lost (called→not)"),
         grp = factor(grp, levels = FATES),
         fbin_a = cut(f_alt_a, breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.2), include.lowest = TRUE, labels = BINS),
         # mismapped-OUT: reads whose TRUE span covers p but are mapped elsewhere/unmapped -- the
         # mirror of mismapped-in (foreign reads AT p). From the truth-centric ledger cells.
         mmout_a = mm_clip_a + mm_noclip_a + dc_a + un_a,
         mmout_b = mm_clip_b + mm_noclip_b + dc_b + un_b)
flip <- filter(pairs, grp == "flip (→called)")

# per-SNP distribution boxplots by fate, for one divergence (depth included; a SEPARATE figure per D
# rather than another facet dimension, which would be too busy)
METS <- c("depth at p", "f_alt", "ref reads at p", "mismapped-in ref", "mismapped-out",
          "mean MAPQ at p", "neighbor unrec SNPs (±200bp)")
distfig <- function(dd) {
  d1 <- filter(pairs, grp %in% FATES, divergence == dd) %>% mutate(id = row_number())
  bind_rows(
    d1 %>% transmute(id, caller, grp, metric = "depth at p",       before = depth_p_a,   after = depth_p_b),
    d1 %>% transmute(id, caller, grp, metric = "f_alt",            before = f_alt_a,      after = f_alt_b),
    d1 %>% transmute(id, caller, grp, metric = "ref reads at p",   before = ref_p_a,      after = ref_p_b),
    d1 %>% transmute(id, caller, grp, metric = "mismapped-in ref", before = mmin_ref_p_a, after = mmin_ref_p_b),
    d1 %>% transmute(id, caller, grp, metric = "mismapped-out",    before = mmout_a,      after = mmout_b),
    d1 %>% transmute(id, caller, grp, metric = "mean MAPQ at p",   before = mapq_p_a,     after = mapq_p_b),
    d1 %>% transmute(id, caller, grp, metric = "neighbor unrec SNPs (±200bp)", before = nb_unrec_a, after = nb_unrec_b)) %>%
    pivot_longer(c(before, after), names_to = "state", values_to = "value") %>%
    mutate(state = factor(state, levels = c("before", "after")), metric = factor(metric, levels = METS)) %>%
    ggplot(aes(state, value, fill = caller)) +
    geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.2, outlier.alpha = 0.2, linewidth = 0.28,
                 position = position_dodge(0.8), width = 0.7) +
    facet_grid(metric ~ grp, scales = "free_y") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = corecol(pal = "wilke", numcol = 3), name = "caller") +
    labs(x = "earlier → later iteration", y = NULL,
         title = sprintf("Per-SNP pileup DISTRIBUTIONS by fate — s01, D=%s", format(dd))) +
    bartheme() +
    theme(strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0), panel.spacing = unit(0.85, "lines"),
          panel.border = element_rect(color = "grey75", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.4),
          strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey92", color = "grey75", linewidth = 0.4))
}

# mean trend across divergences for ONE fate (a compact direction-of-change view; one figure per fate)
labA <- c(depth = "depth at p", ref = "ref reads at p", mminref = "mismapped-in ref",
          mmout = "mismapped-out", mapq = "mean MAPQ at p", falt = "f_alt",
          nbunrec = "neighbor unrec SNPs (±200bp)")
meantrend <- function(g) {
  filter(pairs, grp == g) %>% group_by(caller, divergence) %>%
    summarize(depth_a = mean(depth_p_a), depth_b = mean(depth_p_b), ref_a = mean(ref_p_a), ref_b = mean(ref_p_b),
              mminref_a = mean(mmin_ref_p_a), mminref_b = mean(mmin_ref_p_b),
              mmout_a = mean(mmout_a), mmout_b = mean(mmout_b), mapq_a = mean(mapq_p_a), mapq_b = mean(mapq_p_b),
              falt_a = mean(f_alt_a), falt_b = mean(f_alt_b),
              nbunrec_a = mean(nb_unrec_a), nbunrec_b = mean(nb_unrec_b), .groups = "drop") %>%
    pivot_longer(matches("_(a|b)$"), names_pattern = "(.+)_([ab])$", names_to = c("metric", ".value")) %>%
    mutate(metric = factor(labA[metric], levels = unname(labA))) %>%
    pivot_longer(c(a, b), names_to = "state", values_to = "value") %>%
    mutate(state = factor(ifelse(state == "a", "earlier", "later"), levels = c("earlier", "later"))) %>%
    ggplot(aes(state, value, group = caller, color = caller)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.85) + geom_point(size = 2.2) +
    facet_grid(metric ~ divergence, scales = "free_y", labeller = labeller(divergence = label_both)) +
    scale_color_manual(values = corecol(pal = "wilke", numcol = 3), name = "caller") +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "group mean", title = sprintf("MEAN pileup by divergence — %s", g)) +
    bartheme() +
    theme(strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0), panel.spacing = unit(1, "lines"),
          panel.border = element_rect(color = "grey75", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.4),
          strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey92", color = "grey75", linewidth = 0.4))
}

Per-SNP distributions (boxplots, not means), one figure per divergence for the three fates. Each box is the spread of that pileup axis over all SNPs in the fate at the earlier vs later iteration; the median line and IQR show how wide the variation really is behind any single mean. depth at p is included and is roughly flat across the flip — foreign reads leave as the true reads arrive.

distfig(0.06)

distfig(0.08)

distfig(0.10)

The mean trend across divergences, one figure per fate — the compact direction-of-change view (each point a group mean; the boxplots above show the spread). In flips every contamination axis falls while f_alt/MAPQ rise; stayed called is flat and clean at every divergence; stayed not-called stays contaminated throughout — the sites iteration cannot fix.

meantrend("flip (→called)")

meantrend("stayed called")

meantrend("stayed not-called")

Finally, the flips by starting f_alt bin (D=0.10, group means). Left: f_alt before vs after — the top bin is flat while low bins migrate up (alt support re-anchors). Right: the mismapped-in ref contamination that clears, present in every bin.

labB <- c(falt = "f_alt (before vs after)", mminref = "mismapped-in ref reads at p")
flip %>% filter(divergence == 0.10) %>% group_by(caller, fbin_a) %>%
  summarize(falt_a = mean(f_alt_a), falt_b = mean(f_alt_b),
            mminref_a = mean(mmin_ref_p_a), mminref_b = mean(mmin_ref_p_b), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_longer(c(falt_a, falt_b, mminref_a, mminref_b),
               names_pattern = "(.+)_([ab])$", names_to = c("metric", ".value")) %>%
  mutate(metric = factor(labB[metric], levels = unname(labB))) %>%
  pivot_longer(c(a, b), names_to = "state", values_to = "value") %>%
  mutate(state = factor(ifelse(state == "a", "before (uncalled)", "after (called)"),
                        levels = c("before (uncalled)", "after (called)"))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(fbin_a, value, color = caller, linetype = state, group = interaction(caller, state))) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.85) + geom_point(size = 2.1) +
  facet_wrap(~ metric, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_color_manual(values = corecol(pal = "wilke", numcol = 3), name = "caller") +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c("before (uncalled)" = "22", "after (called)" = "solid"), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "starting f_alt bin (iteration where still uncalled)", y = NULL,
       title = "Flip SNPs by starting f_alt bin (D=0.10, group means)") +
  bartheme() +
  theme(panel.spacing = unit(1.4, "lines"),
        panel.border = element_rect(color = "grey75", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.4),
        strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey92", color = "grey75", linewidth = 0.4))

3.6.4.1 The gatk signature: flips with an unchanged pileup

The most striking pattern is gatk: almost nothing about the pileup at p changes when a gatk SNP flips to called. Two ways to see it (D=0.10). First, how often the pileup was already clean before the flip (clean = f_alt≥0.8, ≤2 ref reads, MAPQ≥50, ≤2 mismapped-in — indistinguishable from a called site):

pairs %>% filter(divergence == 0.10, grp == "flip (→called)") %>%
  mutate(already_clean = f_alt_a >= 0.8 & ref_p_a <= 2 & mapq_p_a >= 50 & mmin_ref_p_a <= 2) %>%
  group_by(caller) %>%
  summarize(`n flips` = n(),
            `pileup already clean before flip` = sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * mean(already_clean)),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  kable(caption = "Fraction of flip SNPs whose pileup at p already looked called-ready before the flip.",
        table.attr = 'class="center"')
Fraction of flip SNPs whose pileup at p already looked called-ready before the flip.
caller n flips pileup already clean before flip
gatk 3174 65%
bcftools 509 1%
freebayes 530 1%

Second, how much each axis actually moves across the flip (mean absolute change):

pairs %>% filter(divergence == 0.10, grp == "flip (→called)") %>%
  group_by(caller) %>%
  summarize(`Δ depth` = round(mean(abs(depth_p_b - depth_p_a)), 1),
            `Δ ref` = round(mean(abs(ref_p_b - ref_p_a)), 1),
            `Δ mismap-in` = round(mean(abs(mmin_ref_p_b - mmin_ref_p_a)), 1),
            `Δ MAPQ` = round(mean(abs(mapq_p_b - mapq_p_a)), 1),
            `Δ f_alt` = round(mean(abs(f_alt_b - f_alt_a)), 2), .groups = "drop") %>%
  kable(caption = "Mean absolute change in each pileup axis across the flip.",
        table.attr = 'class="center"')
Mean absolute change in each pileup axis across the flip.
caller Δ depth Δ ref Δ mismap-in Δ MAPQ Δ f_alt
gatk 1.4 0.6 0.6 2.6 0.05
bcftools 9.4 6.3 5.3 31.0 0.37
freebayes 9.5 5.5 5.1 30.6 0.35

For ~65% of gatk flips the pileup at p is already clean before the flip and barely moves (MAPQ shifts ~2.6, f_alt ~0.05) — versus ~1% for the pileup callers, whose flips move everything (MAPQ ~31, f_alt ~0.37). gatk is not freed by a better pileup at the SNP; its reads were presentable all along. Recovery must come from off p — the reference-anchored reassembler finally closing the local haplotype once the surrounding consensus has converged, a change invisible to any at-p measurement (quantified next).

3.6.4.2 What changes off p: the local unrecovered-SNP load

If the change is in the neighborhood, we can measure it. For each SNP we count the other true hom-div SNPs within ±200 bp (roughly HaplotypeCaller’s active-region + assembly window) that are not yet recovered into the consensus at that iteration — the local mismatch load the reference-anchored reassembler must bridge to find shared exact k-mers and close a haplotype (analyses/lib/neighborhood_assembly.py via run_neighborhood.sh, results/neighborhood/).

nb <- read_csv("analyses/s01-baseline-iterative/results/neighborhood/neighborhood-summary.csv",
               col_types = cols())
fcol <- c("stayed called" = "#4d9221", "flip (→called)" = "#e08214", "stayed not-called" = "#b2182b")
nb %>% filter(divergence == 0.10, fate %in% c("flip", "stayed_notcalled", "stayed_called")) %>%
  transmute(caller = factor(caller, levels = c("gatk", "bcftools", "freebayes")),
            fate = factor(fate, levels = c("stayed_called", "flip", "stayed_notcalled"),
                          labels = names(fcol)),
            before = mean_unrecovered_before, after = mean_unrecovered_after) %>%
  pivot_longer(c(before, after), names_to = "state", values_to = "unrec") %>%
  mutate(state = factor(state, levels = c("before", "after"))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(state, unrec, color = fate, group = fate)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) + geom_point(size = 2.8) +
  facet_wrap(~ caller) +
  scale_color_manual(values = fcol, name = "fate") +
  labs(x = "earlier → later iteration", y = "unrecovered neighbor\nhom-div SNPs (±200 bp)",
       title = "The assemblable neighborhood: local unrecovered-SNP load, D=0.10") +
  bartheme() + theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 11))

This is the answer. For flips the local unrecovered-SNP load collapses — gatk 25→6 at D=0.10 — into the range where already-called sites live (~4), while stayed-not-called neighborhoods stay cluttered (31→30) and never assemble, which is exactly why they never flip. The same collapse drives the pileup callers’ flips (20→3): the common upstream cause is the local consensus converging, which lowers the neighborhood’s divergence to the reference. It simply acts through a different bottleneck — assembly for gatk (whose reads at p were already presentable), read placement for bcftools/freebayes (letting the contaminating reads at p map to their true homes). One cause, two effects — the assembler-vs-alignment split, measured directly.

Interpretation. First the caution the distributions make plain (Figure 1): these groups are strongly right-skewed, so means overstate the typical SNP — the bcftools flip group averages ~8 ref reads at D=0.10 but the median flip SNP has 5 (IQR 0–15), and many start with none. With that in mind the three fates separate cleanly:

  • stayed called (the large control): clean at both iterations — ~0 ref reads, f_alt≈1. These were never contaminated; nothing needs to change.
  • flip (→called): contaminated → clean. Ref reads at p clear (median 5→0) and, in lockstep, the mismapped-out reads that belong at p come home (5→0) — the SNP’s own reads return as the foreign ref reads leave, and MAPQ rises. The ref reads are almost entirely mismapped-in (foreign): the mismapped-in count tracks the ref count nearly one-to-one.
  • stayed not-called: the contamination persists — ref reads stay ~15, mismapped-out stays ~17, f_alt stays ≈0 across the iteration. These are the genuinely hard sites (repetitive / multi-mapping neighborhoods) the consensus can’t disentangle, which is why they never flip.

So a flip is exactly the event where a contaminated pileup resolves — foreign reads out, true reads in — while stayed-not-called SNPs are where it doesn’t. By starting f_alt bin (Figure 3) the flips split into two routes: top-bin flips keep f_alt flat and are pure contamination cleanup; low-bin flips migrate up in f_alt as their true-alt reads re-anchor. gatk shows the smallest pileup changes and the largest f_alt migration — its deficit is the reassembler (freed by a converged neighborhood), whereas bcftools/freebayes are freed chiefly by the pileup clearing. (Script: scripts/vrf_pileup_decomp.R; --pileup columns depth_p, ref_p, alt_p, oth_p, mapq_p, mapq20_p and mismapped-in mmin_p, mmin_ref_p, mmin_alt_p; mismapped-out = mm_clip+mm_noclip+dc+un.)

Note on the f_alt≈0 not-called band: these are not unsimulated sites. The truth-site check (under SNP recovery) finds every truth SNP present in its reads, so f_alt≈0 means the reads that carry the alt did not arrive at the site (lost, mismapped or clipped): a mapping loss, not a missing allele.

4 Heterozygous site recovery

Het sites (true 0/1) are the classic allelic-dropout target of reference bias: when a het’s alt-bearing reads map poorly, the site looks homozygous-reference. They are never baked into the (haploid) consensus, so this is scored from the raw per-iteration caller VCF vs truth — het_tp / n_truth_het.

The D = 0 point is the germline-calling baseline. At zero divergence the task reduces to ordinary diploid variant calling against a matching reference — the well-benchmarked regime — with only het sites and sequencing error in play. Our pipeline hits ~99% het recall with ~150 false positives there (see the divergence = 0 column below), a sane germline anchor and the point where the sim can eventually be checked against real-data truth (Genome-in-a-Bottle; logged as a separate calibration). Everything to the right of it is the reference-bias departure from that baseline as divergence grows. (Divergence recall necessarily starts at D > 0 — at D = 0 there are no divergent sites to recover — and the near-0 anchors 0.001/0.005 extend that curve toward the origin.)

ggplot(hets, aes(x = factor(divergence), y = m, color = iteration)) +
  geom_line(aes(group = divergence), color = "grey65", size = 0.6) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = m - s, ymax = m + s), width = 0.0015) +
  geom_point(size = 2.6) +
  facet_wrap(~caller) +
  scale_x_discrete(guide = guide_axis(angle = 45)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  scale_color_manual(values = cols, name = "Iteration") +
  xlab("Simulated divergence (D)") + ylab("Heterozygous-site recall") +
  bartheme() + theme(legend.position = "bottom")

Interpretation. Het recall behaves almost exactly like the divergence recall — same caller ordering, same iteration rescue, and per caller the two nearly coincide (at D=0.10 single-shot: gatk het 69% vs div 70%; bcftools het 97% vs div 98%). So het reference bias is not a uniform evidence effect. It splits into (1) a small, caller-independent allelic-dropout tax — the pileup callers sit ~1 point below their own divergence recall (99.2% → ~97% as D rises), the genuine case where a het’s alt reads are clipped/unmapped; iteration restores it; and (2) a large, gatk-specific loss that mirrors its homozygous divergence deficit — het sites in divergent regions are missed by the same reassembly failure that loses the homozygous divergent SNPs, and recovered the same way as effective divergence falls. For the assembler, a het in a divergent window is lost for the same reason a homozygous divergent SNP is.

5 Summary

  • Iterative mapping recovers more true divergence — recall rises every iteration and converges by ~3 rounds.
  • The benefit is largest where single-shot is weakest: negligible for the pileup/ haplotype callers already near ceiling, but a large lift for gatk at high divergence (single-shot 70.4% → iterated 81.0% at D=0.10; 3 seeds, SD <0.1 pt). The fate bars show the same thing as a shrinking “lost to reference” band.
  • Heterozygous sites recover the same way: het recall closely tracks divergence recall per caller (gatk ~69%→80% at D=0.10; pileup callers ~97%→99.5%), so het reference bias is dominated by the same assembler mechanism — plus a small caller-independent allelic-dropout tax that iteration also restores.
  • This is a caller, not a mapping, effect: single-shot read placement is caller-independent (identical iter1 bars), yet gatk recovers the fewest SNPs — so its deficit is the reference-anchored assembler. As the consensus converges, reads map more exactly (gatk soft-clip 40%→10% at D=0.10), a readout of falling effective divergence that both tracks and feeds the recovery.

Scope: chr19, SNP-only, 30×. Open question: how far does iteration go — does recall plateau below 100%, and is the residual the repeat/mapping-limited floor? (Test with more iterations + a convergence diagnostic.) Indels + liftover are s02.
